title: improv·artist · thread (Chiharu Shiota)
mutation_directive: improv artist: thread via Chiharu Shiota

improv_extras.practice: rooms filled with red or black thread; memory webs, suspended objects

v1.feedback: The Shiota reference lands — red thread web radiating from a dress silhouette to room-scale anchors, suspended keys caught in the mesh, deep crimson on near-black. The dress profile function is well-shaped and the 4500 thread lines should read as a coherent installation. Main risk: base alpha is 0.08 without mic energy, so the piece may render near-invisible until the user grants audio — add a floor energy or idle breath so the threads glow at rest. The suspended keys could use a faint warm-white tint to separate them from the red web, the way Shiota's brass keys catch light differently from the thread.

v2.feedback: The Shiota concept lands well — dress silhouette, radiating crimson threads to room-scale anchors, suspended keys, and the breath-reactive tremor are all legit references. Main issue: threads rendered as GL_POINTS with only 12 segments each will read as dotted constellations rather than taut continuous filaments; switch to THREE.Line or a screen-space line shader (MeshLine) to get that tensile thread quality that defines Shiota's work. The keys at 60 particles each are too small to register as recognizable objects — consider a tiny cross or loop glyph via an SDF in the fragment shader so they read as key silhouettes caught in the web.
